description: Our team Ryoga his mother and Hinata is dedicated to solving the energy and water challenges brought by the region's massive AI data center boom. Inspired by real-world experiences with Atmospheric Water Generation (AWG) in Japan, we created the Aqua-Thermo Loop. By combining solar power, server heat recovery, and air-to-water technology, our solution eliminates blackouts, preserves local water, and empowers communities to thrive alongside next-generation AI infrastructure.
summary: Aqua Thermo Loop is an interactive NASA POWER trend explorer for Paraguay. Users select temperature, relative humidity or solar radiation, compare four geographic references over 2001–2024, inspect annual and monthly values, quantify change with Sen slopes, and review exploratory significance diagnostics. Original NASA JSON, retrieval timestamps, source queries and downloadable analyses make the evidence traceable. A separate 3D concept connects these environmental questions to a proposed AI data center near ZUNZ Substation. The campus is unbuilt, its parcel is undefined, and no engineering performance or autonomous operation is validated. The project helps students, educators and technically interested users distinguish a visible slope from statistically supported evidence of change.
details:
• We developed a browser-based tool for the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge. NASA POWER provides monthly and annual temperature (T2M), relative humidity (RH2M), direct-normal solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DNI) and global-horizontal solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) for the proposed-site reference near ZUNZ, Colonia Yguazú, Ciudad del Este and Asunción. POWER distributes meteorological reanalysis from MERRA-2 and solar products derived from CERES SYN1deg.

Users choose a variable, reference and time window, compare annual time series and geographic markers, inspect twelve monthly values, and download CSV, original NASA JSON or a reproducible analysis/provenance JSON. Missing values are excluded without interpolation. Valid NASA annual means are used only when all constituent months are present. Inference requires at least fifteen contiguous complete years. When the API fails, an explicitly labelled verified archive preserves access to the original records; no synthetic replacement measurements are generated.

The custom exploratory analysis uses Sen slope, a tie/continuity-corrected Mann–Kendall diagnostic and a circular block bootstrap of detrended residuals (999 draws). The larger diagnostic p-value is adjusted with Benjamini–Hochberg across sixteen reference-variable tests for the selected period. For archived ZUNZ temperature in 2001–2024, Sen slope is approximately +0.275 °C per decade and q is approximately 0.801; this is insufficient evidence of a significant trend under the selected method, not evidence that no change exists. No default test meets q < 0.05. Source-grid overlap, short series and repeated period selection limit inference; q is not a probability that the trend is false.

The geographic journey and clickable 3D equipment illustrate a possible future context for solar energy, thermal storage, water collection, liquid cooling and waste-heat recovery. They are explanatory diagrams, not a numerical physics model. NASA environmental records do not validate CSP electricity production, AWG water yield, ORC net output, land ownership, approved grid connections, water self-sufficiency or autonomous control. ZUNZ coordinates reference the substation, not a surveyed campus parcel. Asunción is a comparison outside Alto Paraná. ZUNZ and Yguazú share identical bundled grid series and are not independent local measurements.

The project uses Next.js, TypeScript, React, Three.js, React Three Fiber/Drei and Leaflet. GitHub stores the source and Vercel hosts the web application. Real NASA data are central to the trend explorer; the engineering concept remains separate and unvalidated. The intended benefit is transparent learning and preliminary environmental exploration, not engineering certification or climate attribution. NASA data use does not imply NASA endorsement.
